Reproducing Simmons et al. (2026) from dandiset 001777¶

Paper. Simmons DV, ..., Surmeier DJ (2026). Astrocytes mediate the dopaminergic modulation of tonic GABAergic signaling in substantia nigra. Science Advances 12, eadq8840. doi:10.1126/sciadv.adq8840. The claims file (claims/simmons-2026.yaml) was written from the version of record and its supplement.

Dandiset. DANDI:001777, version 0.260521.2201 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001777/0.260521.2201). The paper cites no dandiset version; this is the only published version, so it is pinned. The draft has the same 412 assets and size.

What the dandiset holds. 412 NWB files of SNr recordings (Clampex files converted one to one), each sweep a VoltageClampSeries in pA at 20 kHz: cell-attached spiking before and after bath drugs, and whole-cell evoked IPSCs. What each file is (virus, drugs, which file is the control) is written only in the free-text notes of each file, which the helper parses. There are no SNc recordings, no recordings at room temperature, in low glucose, with SCH39166, NPPB, or Gq-DREADD, no gabazine-then-quinpirole recordings, and no imaging, RNAscope or voltammetry.

Method common to the rate claims (claims file, M1 to M6). Spikes are detected in each sweep by threshold on the high-passed current (snr.detect_spikes; the paper used Clampfit with settings it does not give). A cell's rate in a condition is the median of its per-episode rates under two readings of the stable window: (a) all episodes, (b) for a drug the episodes from 6 min after the start of the drug's file. Percent change is given under the three readings of M2. Tests are two-sided paired t tests unless the claim names another; one-sided P and the Wilcoxon test are shown as variants. Every rate result is also shown at detection thresholds of 6 and 12 noise units, and without the seven recordings whose spikes vanish during the experiment (data check), and for the two Fig. 7F claims without an eighth found by inspection.

import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import snr

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 400)
pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 80)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
assets = snr.list_assets()
meta = snr.survey(assets)
files = snr.build_files(meta)
cells = snr.build_cells(files)
F = files.set_index("path")
print(f"{len(assets)} assets in dandiset {snr.DANDISET} version {snr.VERSION}; metadata read in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

412 assets in dandiset 001777 version 0.260521.2201; metadata read in 66 s

Data check¶

Each check of the metadata against the values is stated under its output.

Every pair of files with the same session id and an obj- suffix holds the same data; each is counted once. Three subject ids carry recordings on dates 4 to 32 days apart, with ages that advance with the date. Brain-slice experiments end the animal, so either the ids were reused or the dates are wrong; this is recorded as a finding and does not change the counts, which are of cells.

The grouping follows the notes: the control file and the file the drug was applied in, by their original Clampex numbers. Three notes are inconsistent with their files: file 0007 of subject 8952 and file 0000 of subject 6813 (Five stim) are not named in their own notes, and the nine files 0015 to 0023 of subject 9019 carry the notes of files 0003 to 0010 of the same day (a second cell), so which of them were recorded in quinpirole is not stated. That cell is left out of the main IPSC analysis and shown as a variant.

The counts of cells match the paper's n for most experiments: Fig. 2C 8, Fig. 4A 4, Fig. 4B 5, Fig. 5E 15 shRNA, Fig. 5H 5, Fig. 6A 9, Fig. 6C 8, Fig. 6E 6, Fig. 7D 10, Fig. 7E 11, Fig. 7F 19, Fig. 7H 6. Disulfiram with gabazine has 3 cells against the paper's 5, quinpirole without an opsin 7 against 8 (Fig. 3A), and gabazine alone 49 against 45 (Fig. 3B legend).

gf = cells[cells.family == "gap-free"]
rows = []
for _, c in gf.iterrows():
    for role in ["ctrl", "drug1", "drug2", "both"]:
        for p in c[role]:
            rows.append(dict(cell=c["cell"], experiment=c["experiment"], role=role, file=f"{num[p]:04d}",
                             start=F.loc[p, "start"].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                             minutes=round(F.loc[p, "sweep_len"] / snr.FS / 60, 1)))
gfr = pd.DataFrame(rows)
end = pd.to_datetime(gfr.start) + pd.to_timedelta(gfr.minutes * 60, unit="s")
gfr["gap_after_previous_file_s"] = np.where(gfr.cell == gfr.cell.shift(), (pd.to_datetime(gfr.start) - end.shift()).dt.total_seconds().round(0), np.nan)
print(f"Gap-free files ({len(gfr)}) grouped by cell, in order of start time; the gap is from the end of the cell's previous file:")
print(gfr.to_string(index=False))
g = gfr.gap_after_previous_file_s.dropna()
print(f"Gaps between the files of one cell: {len(g)}, from {g.min():.0f} to {g.max():.0f} s")
print("\nNotes of each gap-free cell (from its first file), which name its control and drug files:")
for _, c in gf.iterrows():
    p = (c["ctrl"] + c["both"] + c["drug1"])[0]
    print(f"{c['cell']}: {F.loc[p, 'pnotes']}")

Spike detection¶

The rate claims rest on spike detection. The next cell detects spikes in every sweep of the cell-attached files (about ten minutes) and shows, on two sweeps of each experiment, the amplitudes of the threshold crossings in noise units: in most files noise events sit below about 8 and action currents above about 10, which is why 8 is the main threshold.

In [6]:
t = time.time()
rate_exps = [e for e in cells.experiment.unique() if not e.startswith(("gpe_opto", "gpe_gi_ipsc"))]
rate_paths = sorted({p for _, r in cells[cells.experiment.isin(rate_exps)].iterrows()
                     for k in ["ctrl", "drug1", "drug2", "both"] for p in r[k]})
spikes = snr.all_spikes([F.loc[p, "asset_id"] for p in rate_paths])
import resource
print(f"spikes detected in {len(rate_paths)} files in {time.time() - t:.0f} s; "
      f"peak memory of workers {resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss / 1e6:.2f} GB")

In [7]:
import h5py, remfile
from scipy import signal as _sig
rows = []
for exp in sorted(rate_exps):
    c = cells[cells.experiment == exp].iloc[0]
    p = (c["ctrl"] or c["both"])[0]
    f = h5py.File(remfile.File(snr.asset_url(F.loc[p, "asset_id"])), "r")
    a = f["acquisition"]
    key = sorted(a)[0]
    x = a[key]["data"][: int(60 * snr.FS)].astype(float)
    y = _sig.sosfiltfilt(snr._SOS, x)
    noise = np.median(np.abs(y)) / 0.6745
    pol = spikes[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]["polarity"]
    idx, _, _ = snr.detect_spikes(x, 4.0, pol)
    z = np.array([(pol * y[i:i + 40]).max() for i in idx]) / noise
    h = np.histogram(z, bins=[4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 30, 1e9])[0]
    rows.append(dict(experiment=exp, file=p.split("/")[1][:34], noise_pA=round(noise, 2), polarity=pol,
                     **{f"z{a}-{b}": n for a, b, n in zip([4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 30], [6, 8, 10, 15, 30, "inf"], h)}))
print("Crossings of 4 noise units in the first sweep (or first 60 s) of one control file per experiment, by peak amplitude in noise units:")
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

In most files the crossings split into a group under 8 and a group above 10 to 15 noise units, but not in all: in the shRNA, SNAP-5114 and astrocytic Gi-DREADD with gabazine files above, many crossings lie between 8 and 10, so there is no clean gap at 8 everywhere. The rate results below are repeated at 6 and 12, and every cell's rates at the three thresholds are printed next.

In [8]:
def rates(reading="a", k=snr.K_THRESH, window=None, note_windows=False, exps=None, cl=None):
    cl = cells if cl is None else cl
    if exps is not None:
        cl = cl[cl.experiment.isin(exps)]
    return snr.cell_rates(cl, F, spikes, reading=reading, k=k, window=window, note_windows=note_windows)


def summarize(exps, a="ctrl", b="drug1", window=None, readings=("a", "b"), ks=snr.THRESHOLDS, cl=None, note_windows=False):
    out = []
    for r in readings:
        for k in ks:
            d = rates(r, k, window, note_windows, exps, cl)
            s = snr.paired_summary(d, a, b)
            out.append(dict(reading=r, k=k, **s))
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def by_subject(d, a="ctrl", b="drug1"):
    g = d.dropna(subset=[a, b]).groupby("subject")
    return pd.DataFrame({"cells": g.size(), f"{a}_mean": g[a].mean(), f"{b}_mean": g[b].mean(),
                         "cells_up": g.apply(lambda x: int((x[b] > x[a]).sum()))})


all_rates = rates("a", exps=rate_exps)
print("Rates (Hz, reading a, threshold 8) by experiment: median and range of control rates")
print(all_rates.groupby("experiment").ctrl.describe()[["count", "min", "50%", "max"]].round(1).to_string())

Detection threshold and failed recordings¶

Every cell's rate in each condition at the three thresholds (reading a), so that the cells whose rate depends on the threshold can be seen. Then the cells whose rate in a condition falls under a quarter of their rate in the condition before (snr.failed_cells, under either reading of M1), with the time course of their rate and of the amplitude of the threshold crossings.

In [9]:
side = {k: rates("a", k, exps=rate_exps) for k in snr.THRESHOLDS}
tab = side[snr.K_THRESH][["cell", "experiment"]].copy()
for cond in ["ctrl", "drug1", "drug2"]:
    for k in snr.THRESHOLDS:
        tab[f"{cond}_k{k:g}"] = side[k][cond].round(2)
tab = tab.dropna(axis=1, how="all")
print("Rate (Hz, reading a) of every cell at thresholds 6, 8 and 12:")
print(tab.sort_values(["experiment", "cell"]).to_string(index=False))
spread = pd.concat([(side[6.0][c] - side[12.0][c]).abs() / side[8.0][c].clip(lower=1) for c in ["ctrl", "drug1", "drug2"]], axis=1).max(1)
print(f"\nCells in which some condition's rate differs by more than 25% between thresholds 6 and 12: "
      f"{int((spread > 0.25).sum())} of {len(spread)}")
print(tab[spread.to_numpy() > 0.25].to_string(index=False))

ok_cells = cells[~cells.cell.isin(list(failed))]

CI = cells.set_index("cell")


def time_courses(which):
    """Plot and print the rate and the crossing amplitude of each cell in `which` (cell: experiment)."""
    rows = []
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(which), figsize=(3.2 * max(len(which), 2), 3), sharey=True)
    for ax, (cell, exp) in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), which.items()):
        c = CI.loc[cell]
        paths = c["ctrl"] + c["drug1"] + c["drug2"]
        t00 = min(F.loc[p, "start"] for p in paths)
        for role in ["ctrl", "drug1", "drug2"]:
            for p in c[role]:
                sp = spikes[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]
                r, t = snr.episode_rates(sp, snr.K_THRESH)
                amp = snr.episode_amplitudes(sp, 6.0) / np.median(sp["noise"])
                tm = (t + (F.loc[p, "start"] - t00).total_seconds()) / 60
                ax.plot(tm, r, "k.", ms=2)
                ax2 = ax.twinx()
                ax2.plot(tm, amp, "r.", ms=2)
                ax2.set_ylim(0, 120)
                for m0 in np.arange(np.floor(tm.min() / 2) * 2, tm.max(), 2):
                    s = (tm >= m0) & (tm < m0 + 2)
                    if s.any():
                        rows.append(dict(cell=cell, experiment=exp, condition=role, file=f"{num[p]:04d}", minute=int(m0),
                                         rate_hz=round(float(r[s].mean()), 2),
                                         amp_noise_units=round(float(np.nanmedian(amp[s])), 1) if np.isfinite(amp[s]).any() else np.nan))
        ax.set_title(f"{cell}\n{exp}", fontsize=8)
        ax.set_xlabel("min from control start")
    np.atleast_1d(axes)[0].set_ylabel("rate (Hz, black)")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    tcf = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    print("Rate (threshold 8) and median amplitude of the threshold-6 crossings (noise units), in 2-min bins:")
    print(tcf.to_string(index=False))
    print("Plotted ranges: rate", round(float(tcf.rate_hz.min()), 1), "to", round(float(tcf.rate_hz.max()), 1),
          "Hz (2-min means; single episodes up to", round(float(max(snr.episode_rates(spikes[F.loc[p, 'asset_id']], snr.K_THRESH)[0].max()
          for cell in which for p in CI.loc[cell, 'ctrl'] + CI.loc[cell, 'drug1'] + CI.loc[cell, 'drug2'])), 1),
          "Hz); amplitude axis 0 to 120 noise units, points above it:",
          int(sum((snr.episode_amplitudes(spikes[F.loc[p, 'asset_id']], 6.0) / np.median(spikes[F.loc[p, 'asset_id']]['noise']) > 120).sum()
              for cell in which for p in CI.loc[cell, 'ctrl'] + CI.loc[cell, 'drug1'] + CI.loc[cell, 'drug2'])))


time_courses(failed)


def without_failed(exps, **kw):
    return summarize(exps, cl=ok_cells, **kw)

Twenty-seven of 171 cells have a condition whose rate differs by more than 25% between thresholds 6 and 12; the outcomes are given at all three. Seven cells fall to under a quarter of their rate in the condition before: 5110-2020-10-20-15 (quinpirole without opsin), 6808-2022-05-31-45 (disulfiram then gabazine), 6812-2022-06-09-49 (DEAB then gabazine), 7084-2022-11-28-73 (shRNA), 7310-2023-01-06-84 and 7324-2023-02-22-93 (gabazine) and 8797-2025-03-12-123 (astrocytic Gi-DREADD, gabazine then CNO). In each, the amplitude of the crossings falls to about 6 to 7 noise units, the size of noise crossings at a threshold of 6, by the time the rate falls, so the action currents are no longer seen. In 5110-2020-10-20-15 the amplitude halves during the control file, from 18.5 to 9.8 noise units, before quinpirole. No drug in the paper changes SNr rate by more than about 50%, so these are read as recordings that failed (lost seal or cell), not as drug effects. They are kept in the main tests, as the claims file asks for every cell, and each claim that holds one of them is also given without them (ok_cells).

A cell the quarter rule does not catch¶

8979-2025-05-27-164 (SNAP-5114 then quinpirole) is not caught by the quarter rule, but its rate in SNAP-5114 falls to 0.17 Hz at threshold 12 (rates above). Its time course:

In 8979-2025-05-27-164 the amplitude of the crossings falls during the control file, from 36 to 15 noise units, reaches 7 to 8 noise units, the size of noise crossings, by minute 28 in SNAP-5114, while the rate at threshold 8 falls from 17 to 2 Hz. It stays at about 6 noise units in quinpirole until minute 42, after which crossings of 90 to 150 noise units come and go (a new seal, or another cell). Its SNAP-5114 and quinpirole rates are therefore not measurements of the cell's firing; it is read as a failed recording like the seven above. It is kept in the main tests, and the two fig7f claims are also given without it.

Timing of the light train and of the evoked currents¶

There is no trial or stimulus table: the light and electrical stimuli are not stored (the stimulus series hold only a -10 mV test pulse). The timing is read from the responses. The 30-Hz train of Fig. 2 should silence spiking from 2 to 4 s of each 6-s sweep in the Chronos cells and not in the cells without an opsin; the evoked IPSCs should start at the same time in every cell.

In [12]:
def psth(paths, k=snr.K_THRESH, bins=np.arange(0, 6.0001, 0.1)):
    counts, n = np.zeros(len(bins) - 1), 0
    for p in paths:
        sp = spikes[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]
        for t in sp["spikes"][k]:
            counts += np.histogram(t, bins)[0]
            n += 1
    return counts / n / np.diff(bins), n


bins = np.arange(0, 6.0001, 0.1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3.5), sharey=True)
for i, exp in enumerate(["gpe_train_quinpirole", "quinpirole_no_opsin"]):
    rows = []
    for _, c in cells[cells.experiment == exp].iterrows():
        h, n = psth(c["ctrl"])
        rows.append(h)
        ax[i].plot(bins[:-1] + 0.05, h, lw=0.7)
    rows = np.array(rows)
    pre = rows[:, (bins[:-1] >= 1) & (bins[:-1] < 2)].mean(1)
    on = rows[:, (bins[:-1] >= 2) & (bins[:-1] < 2.2)].mean(1)
    post = rows[:, (bins[:-1] >= 4) & (bins[:-1] < 5)].mean(1)
    print(f"{exp}: control rate 1-2 s {np.round(pre, 1)} Hz; 2.0-2.2 s {np.round(on, 1)}; 4-5 s {np.round(post, 1)}")
    ax[i].set_title(exp)
    ax[i].axvspan(2, 4, color="0.9")
    ax[i].set_xlabel("time in sweep (s)")
ax[0].set_ylabel("rate (Hz)")

In every Chronos cell the rate falls at 2.0 s and recovers by 4 s, and it does not fall in the cells without an opsin: the train runs from 2 to 4 s, as the Fig. 2 legend implies, and the spike times share the clock of the light. The timing of the evoked IPSCs is shown with their analysis.

fig1c-quinpirole-reduces-gpe-ipsc¶

The D2R agonist quinpirole (2 uM) reduces the amplitude of optogenetically evoked GPe IPSCs in SNr neurons by roughly 30%. (paired t test, P = 0.02, n = 5; expected 30 +/- 3%)

The "20 Hz Light" files hold 8 sweeps of 15 s each; a train of 0.5-ms light pulses at 20 Hz starts at 0.55 s (read from the responses below). Amplitude: peak of the mean evoked current over all sweeps of a condition, from the mean over the 20 ms before the first pulse (claims file). The peak is taken within 0.5 to 20 ms after the pulse. Its sign is fixed per cell by its control: the currents are outward in cells held at -50 to -55 mV and inward in the cell held at -70 mV (notes).

In [13]:
ipsc_cells = cells[cells.experiment == "gpe_opto_ipsc_quinpirole"].copy()
ipsc_paths = sorted({p for _, r in ipsc_cells.iterrows() for k in ["ctrl", "drug1", "unlabelled"] for p in r[k]})
t = time.time()
ipsc_X = snr.all_sweeps([F.loc[p, "asset_id"] for p in ipsc_paths], 0.50, 0.70)
print(f"read {len(ipsc_paths)} files in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
STIM1, STIM2 = 0.55, 0.60


def cond_X(paths):
    return np.vstack([ipsc_X[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]["X"] for p in paths])


# the unlabelled second cell of subject 9019: its notes are copies of the first cell's (files 3-6 control,
# 7-10 quinpirole); variant: the same layout shifted to its own files, 15-18 control and 19-22 quinpirole
rows = []
for _, c in ipsc_cells.iterrows():
    if c["unlabelled"]:
        ctrl = [p for p in c["unlabelled"] if 15 <= num[p] <= 18]
        drug = [p for p in c["unlabelled"] if 19 <= num[p] <= 22]
        variant_only = True
    else:
        ctrl, drug, variant_only = c["ctrl"], c["drug1"], False
    Xc, Xd = cond_X(ctrl), cond_X(drug)
    m = Xc.mean(0)
    tt = np.arange(len(m)) / snr.FS + 0.50
    seg = np.abs(m - m[(tt >= 0.53) & (tt < 0.549)].mean())
    onset = tt[(tt > 0.5505) & (seg > 0.2 * seg[(tt > 0.5505) & (tt < 0.57)].max())][0]
    a_c, sign = snr.evoked_amplitudes(Xc, 0.50, STIM1, (-0.02, -0.001), (0.0005, 0.02))
    a_d, _ = snr.evoked_amplitudes(Xd, 0.50, STIM1, (-0.02, -0.001), (0.0005, 0.02), sign)
    # paired-pulse ratio, reading (a): second peak from the baseline before the first pulse
    def second(X, base_ref):
        mm = X.mean(0)
        i = lambda s: int(round((s - 0.50) * snr.FS))
        b = mm[i(base_ref - 0.02 if base_ref == STIM1 else STIM2 - 0.002):i(base_ref - 0.001 if base_ref == STIM1 else STIM2 - 0.0001)].mean()
        seg2 = sign * (mm[i(STIM2 + 0.0005):i(STIM2 + 0.02)] - b)
        return float(seg2.max())
    rows.append(dict(cell=c["cell"], subject=c["subject"], variant_only=variant_only, sign=sign,
                     onset_ms=round(onset * 1000, 2), n_ctrl_sweeps=len(Xc), n_quin_sweeps=len(Xd),
                     amp_ctrl=a_c, amp_quin=a_d, pct_change=(a_d - a_c) / a_c * 100,
                     ppr_a_ctrl=second(Xc, STIM1) / a_c, ppr_a_quin=second(Xd, STIM1) / a_d,
                     ppr_b_ctrl=second(Xc, STIM2) / a_c, ppr_b_quin=second(Xd, STIM2) / a_d,
                     hold=F.loc[(ctrl or drug)[0], "pnotes"].split("Holding potential ")[1][:5]))
ipsc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(ipsc.round(3).to_string(index=False))

def ipsc_test(d, a, b):
    t = stats.ttest_rel(d[b], d[a])
    pc = (d[b] - d[a]) / d[a] * 100
    return dict(n=len(d), mean_a=d[a].mean(), mean_b=d[b].mean(), t=t.statistic, p=t.pvalue,
                p_less=stats.ttest_rel(d[b], d[a], alternative="less").pvalue,
                pct_a_mean_of_cells=pc.mean(), pct_b_of_means=(d[b].mean() - d[a].mean()) / d[a].mean() * 100,
                pct_c_median_of_cells=pc.median())


main = ipsc[~ipsc.variant_only]

                    dict(cells="6 cells (variant: 9019 second cell, files 15-18 / 19-22)", **ipsc_test(ipsc, "amp_ctrl", "amp_quin"))])

Result: reproduced. In the 5 labelled cells the evoked IPSC falls from 265.6 to 198.5 pA in quinpirole (paired t test P = 0.0087), a reduction of 30.1% as the mean of the cells' changes (reading a of M2, inside 30 +/- 3), 25.3% of the group means and 27.3% as the median. With the sixth cell under the assumed file layout, P = 0.0070 and the reduction is 26.7%. The evoked currents start 1.2 to 2.2 ms after 0.55 s in every cell. In the second cell of subject 9019 every one of its nine files, 0015 to 0023, holds an evoked current of 200 to 246 pA, so none of them, file 0023 included, was recorded in gabazine. Files 0015 to 0018 are 5 min apart, then 10 min pass before 0019, which fits a drug applied between 0018 and 0019, the layout assumed for the variant.

fig1e-ppr-rises¶

Quinpirole raises the paired-pulse ratio of GPe evoked IPSCs at a 50 ms interval (paired t test, P = 0.02, n = 6).

Second pulse at 0.60 s, 50 ms after the first. Readings (claims file): (a) second peak from the baseline before the first pulse; (b) second peak from the current in the 2 ms before the second pulse. The paper's n = 6 matches the dataset's six cells only with the second cell of 9019, whose files are labelled by the shifted layout (an assumption, shown with the five labelled cells).

fig2c-quinpirole-attenuates-gpe-inhibition¶

A 2-s, 30-Hz optogenetic train of GPe inputs inhibits SNr spiking, and quinpirole attenuates this inhibition. (Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed rank test, P = 0.02, n = 8)

Percent inhibition = (basal rate - rate in 2 to 4 s) / basal rate x 100 from each condition's PSTH over all its sweeps (claims file; code part 2). Basal: (a) 0 to 2 s; (b) 0 to 2 s and 4 to 6 s. Variant: the median over sweeps of a per-sweep percent inhibition. Both readings of M1 are run: (a) all sweeps of each condition; (b) the quinpirole sweeps from 6 min after the start of its file.

In [17]:
def inhibition(paths, k, basal, t_from=0.0):
    """Percent inhibition from the PSTH of the sweeps starting at t_from (s) or later after the
    start of the condition's first file, and the median of per-sweep percent inhibition."""
    n_sw, cb, ct, per = 0, 0, 0, []
    t_first = F.loc[paths[0], "start"]
    for p in paths:
        sp = spikes[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]
        off = (F.loc[p, "start"] - t_first).total_seconds()
        for t, t0 in zip(sp["spikes"][k], sp["t0"]):
            if t0 + off < t_from:
                continue
            b = sum(np.sum((t >= x0) & (t < x1)) for x0, x1 in basal) / sum(x1 - x0 for x0, x1 in basal)
            tr = np.sum((t >= 2) & (t < 4)) / 2.0
            cb += b; ct += tr; n_sw += 1
            if b > 0:
                per.append((b - tr) / b * 100)
    return (cb - ct) / cb * 100, np.median(per), cb / n_sw, ct / n_sw, n_sw


tc = cells[cells.experiment == "gpe_train_quinpirole"]
res, percell = [], []
for m1, t_from in [("a", 0.0), ("b", snr.DRUG_STABLE_S)]:
    for k in snr.THRESHOLDS:
        for rd, basal in [("a", [(0, 2)]), ("b", [(0, 2), (4, 6)])]:
            rows = []
            for _, c in tc.iterrows():
                ic, icm, bc, trc, nc = inhibition(c["ctrl"], k, basal)
                iq, iqm, bq, trq, nq = inhibition(c["drug1"], k, basal, t_from)
                rows.append(dict(cell=c["cell"], subject=c["subject"], inh_ctrl=ic, inh_quin=iq, inh_ctrl_sweepmed=icm,
                                 inh_quin_sweepmed=iqm, basal_ctrl=bc, train_ctrl=trc, basal_quin=bq, train_quin=trq,
                                 sweeps_ctrl=nc, sweeps_quin=nq))
            d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
            if k == snr.K_THRESH:
                percell.append(d.assign(m1=m1, basal=rd))
            for var, a, b in [("PSTH", "inh_ctrl", "inh_quin"), ("per-sweep median", "inh_ctrl_sweepmed", "inh_quin_sweepmed")]:

                res.append(dict(m1=m1, k=k, basal=rd, measure=var, n=len(d), inh_ctrl=d[a].mean(), inh_quin=d[b].mean(),
                                cells_less_inhibited=int((d[b] < d[a]).sum()), p_wilcoxon=w.pvalue,
                                p_wilcoxon_less=stats.wilcoxon(d[b], d[a], alternative="less").pvalue))

Result: not reproduced. The mean percent inhibition falls from 56.8 to 42.3 in quinpirole (PSTH, basal 0 to 2 s, all sweeps), less inhibition in 5 of 8 cells, but the Wilcoxon test gives P = 0.11 under both readings of the basal window, at every threshold, and P = 0.11 to 0.15 for the per-sweep variant. Under reading b of M1 (quinpirole sweeps from 6 min) the inhibition in quinpirole is 37.1 (basal a), and the test gives P = 0.078 to 0.11 at every threshold and basal window (one-sided 0.039 to 0.055). The direction matches the paper; no two-sided test reaches P < 0.05.

fig2b-inhibition-wanes¶

The GPe train initially suppresses SNr spiking strongly, and the inhibition wanes during the 2-s train.

From each cell's control PSTH, the rate in 2.0 to 2.5 s against 3.5 to 4.0 s (claims file).

In [18]:
rows = []
for k in snr.THRESHOLDS:
    pooled_first = pooled_last = 0
    nsw = 0
    up = 0
    per = []
    for _, c in tc.iterrows():
        f1 = l1 = n = 0
        for p in c["ctrl"]:
            for t in spikes[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]["spikes"][k]:
                f1 += np.sum((t >= 2.0) & (t < 2.5)); l1 += np.sum((t >= 3.5) & (t < 4.0)); n += 1
        per.append((c["cell"], f1 / n / 0.5, l1 / n / 0.5))
        up += l1 > f1
        pooled_first += f1; pooled_last += l1; nsw += n
    rows.append(dict(k=k, cells=len(tc), pooled_rate_first=pooled_first / nsw / 0.5, pooled_rate_last=pooled_last / nsw / 0.5,
                     cells_last_higher=up))
    if k == snr.K_THRESH:
        print(pd.DataFrame(per, columns=["cell", "rate_2.0-2.5", "rate_3.5-4.0"]).round(2).to_string(index=False))

fig3a-quinpirole-increases-rate¶

Quinpirole alone, with no GPe stimulation, raises the basal spike rate of SNr neurons, by about 50% in cell-attached recordings. (paired t test, P < 0.01, n = 8; expected 50 +/- 5%)

Which cells: the Results say the rise was seen "in these experiments" (the Fig. 2 recordings) "in the absence of GPe axon stimulation". The dataset has two sets that fit: (i) 7 cells recorded with the same 30 Hz light protocol in mice with no opsin (no virus in the notes), rate over the whole sweep; (ii) the 8 Chronos cells of Fig. 2, rate over 0 to 2 s, before the train. Both are run.

In the 8 Chronos cells of Fig. 2, before the train, it rises from 20.2 to 24.9 Hz (31.8% as the mean of cells' changes) with P = 0.24 (reading b: 43.2%, P = 0.20). No paired t test gives P < 0.05, under any reading or threshold; the increase of the Chronos cells is near the paper's 50% only under reading b of M1 with reading a of M2 (43.2%). One of the 7 cells without an opsin, 5110-2020-10-20-15, is a failed recording (data check); without it the 6 cells still do not speed up (25.1 to 24.5 Hz, P = 0.53; reading b, -8.9%, P = 0.079).

Result: partially reproduced. Over 49 cells gabazine raises the rate from 21.4 to 23.2 Hz under reading b (paired t test P = 0.047, Wilcoxon P = 0.0044), and from 21.4 to 22.5 Hz under reading a (P = 0.19, Wilcoxon P = 0.023); 31 of 49 cells are faster. The increase is 9.5%, 8.2% and 12.0% (readings a, b, c of M2, reading b of M1), against the paper's 25 +/- 2.5%. At a threshold of 12 no paired t test gives P < 0.05. Two of the 49 cells are failed recordings (7310-2023-01-06-84 and 7324-2023-02-22-93, data check); without them the rise is significant under both readings at thresholds 6 and 8 (reading a P = 0.0097, reading b P = 0.0014 at 8), and is 10.8%, 7.7% and 8.9% (reading a of M1) or 14.2%, 11.2% and 13.5% (reading b). Under reading a of M1 at threshold 8 the increase is 6.3%, 4.9% and 8.8% with all 49 cells, a fifth to a third of the paper's size, and 5.1%, 1.6% and 8.0% at threshold 12; under reading b, or without the two failed recordings, it is a third to a half. The P < 0.05 part rests on an assumption: it holds with all 49 cells only at thresholds 6 and 8 under reading b of M1 (or under both readings without the failed recordings), and not at 12. The gap-free files measured in the windows their notes give (the other cells as reading a) give +9.1%, P = 0.065; the gap-free cells on their own, measured as reading a, give P = 0.20. The notes of 8945-2025-04-16-144 say gabazine was applied during its control file 001, after the baseline window of 300 to 420 s; its rate in that file is 23.5 Hz before 420 s and 23.3 Hz after, so the gabazine did not act within the file, and without the cell the tests are unchanged (reading b P = 0.048 at threshold 8, reading a P = 0.20).

Over 49 cells the change with gabazine is not related to the basal rate: R2 = 0.004 with slope -0.033 (reading a) and R2 = 0.004 with slope 0.037 (reading b), against the paper's R2 = 0.11 and a positive slope; R2 is at most 0.009 at any threshold. Without the two failed recordings R2 is at most 0.028 (47 cells), and the slope is negative under reading a.

fig4a-gpe-gi-dreadd-reduces-ipsc¶

Activating Gi-DREADD in GPe with CNO reduces the amplitude of electrically evoked IPSCs in SNr neurons, similar in size to the quinpirole effect on optogenetically evoked IPSCs. (P = 0.02 in the Results, paired t test P < 0.01 in the legend, n = 4)

The "Five stim" files hold 1-s sweeps with one electrical pulse at 0.40 s (artifact at 0.4002 s). Amplitude as for fig1c: peak of the mean current within 3 to 20 ms after the pulse (after the artifact), from the mean over 0.38 to 0.399 s; sign fixed per cell by its control. Spontaneous action currents (the cells are not fully clamped) fall into some sweeps; the mean is taken over the sweeps without one, and the sign from the clean control sweeps. A sweep holds an action current when its 300 Hz high-passed current exceeds 50 noise units (median absolute deviation / 0.6745 of the high-passed sweep) in 0.38 to 0.45 s outside the artifact (0.3995 to 0.403 s); clean sweeps stay under 50 and action currents are mostly over 100 (printed below), and 100 is shown as a variant. The mean of all sweeps and the median of sweeps are variants.

In [22]:
from scipy import signal as _sig
ec = cells[cells.experiment == "gpe_gi_ipsc_cno"]
paths = sorted({p for _, r in ec.iterrows() for k in ["ctrl", "drug1"] for p in r[k]})
eX = snr.all_sweeps([F.loc[p, "asset_id"] for p in paths], 0.37, 0.45)
keep = np.r_[int(0.010 * snr.FS):int(0.0295 * snr.FS), int(0.033 * snr.FS):int(0.08 * snr.FS)]


def transient(X):
    """Largest high-passed deflection of each sweep outside the artifact, in noise units."""
    hp = _sig.sosfiltfilt(snr._SOS, X, axis=1)
    return np.abs(hp[:, keep]).max(1) / (np.median(np.abs(hp), 1) / 0.6745)


AMP = dict(t0=0.37, stim=0.40, base=(-0.02, -0.001), win=(0.003, 0.02))
rows, hist, traces = [], [], {}
for _, c in ec.iterrows():
    Xc = np.vstack([eX[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]["X"] for p in c["ctrl"]])
    Xd = np.vstack([eX[F.loc[p, "asset_id"]]["X"] for p in c["drug1"]])
    zc, zd = transient(Xc), transient(Xd)
    bins = [0, 10, 20, 35, 50, 75, 100, 200, np.inf]
    hist.append(dict(cell=c["cell"], condition="control", **{f"{a}-{b}": n for a, b, n in zip(bins[:-1], bins[1:], np.histogram(zc, bins)[0])}))
    hist.append(dict(cell=c["cell"], condition="CNO", **{f"{a}-{b}": n for a, b, n in zip(bins[:-1], bins[1:], np.histogram(zd, bins)[0])}))
    row = dict(cell=c["cell"], subject=c["subject"], sweeps_ctrl=len(Xc), sweeps_cno=len(Xd),
               hold=F.loc[c["ctrl"][0], "pnotes"].split("Holding potential ")[1][:5])
    for lim in (50, 100):
        Cc, Cd = Xc[zc <= lim], Xd[zd <= lim]
        a_c, sign = snr.evoked_amplitudes(Cc, AMP["t0"], AMP["stim"], AMP["base"], AMP["win"])
        a_d, _ = snr.evoked_amplitudes(Cd, AMP["t0"], AMP["stim"], AMP["base"], AMP["win"], sign)
        row.update({f"dropped_ctrl_{lim}": int((zc > lim).sum()), f"dropped_cno_{lim}": int((zd > lim).sum()),
                    f"sign_{lim}": sign, f"amp_ctrl_{lim}": a_c, f"amp_cno_{lim}": a_d})
        if lim == 50:
            traces[c["cell"]] = (Cc.mean(0), Cd.mean(0))
    a_c, sign = snr.evoked_amplitudes(Xc, AMP["t0"], AMP["stim"], AMP["base"], AMP["win"])
    a_d, _ = snr.evoked_amplitudes(Xd, AMP["t0"], AMP["stim"], AMP["base"], AMP["win"], sign)
    m_c, _ = snr.evoked_amplitudes(np.median(Xc, 0)[None, :], AMP["t0"], AMP["stim"], AMP["base"], AMP["win"], sign)
    m_d, _ = snr.evoked_amplitudes(np.median(Xd, 0)[None, :], AMP["t0"], AMP["stim"], AMP["base"], AMP["win"], sign)
    row.update(sign_all=sign, amp_ctrl_all=a_c, amp_cno_all=a_d, amp_ctrl_median=m_c, amp_cno_median=m_d)
    rows.append(row)
e4 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Sweeps by largest high-passed deflection outside the artifact (noise units), control and CNO:")
print(pd.DataFrame(hist).fillna(0).to_string(index=False))
print()
print(e4.round(2).T.to_string())
r1 = ipsc_test(main, "amp_ctrl", "amp_quin")
res4 = []
for name, a, b in [("mean of clean sweeps (50)", "amp_ctrl_50", "amp_cno_50"), ("mean of clean sweeps (100)", "amp_ctrl_100", "amp_cno_100"),
                   ("mean of all sweeps", "amp_ctrl_all", "amp_cno_all"), ("median of sweeps", "amp_ctrl_median", "amp_cno_median")]:
    r = ipsc_test(e4, a, b)
    res4.append(dict(measure=name, cells_lower=int((e4[b] < e4[a]).sum()), **r))
res4 = pd.DataFrame(res4)
print()
print(res4.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nQuinpirole reduction (fig1c, 5 cells), readings a, b, c of M2:",
      [round(-r1[k], 1) for k in ["pct_a_mean_of_cells", "pct_b_of_means", "pct_c_median_of_cells"]])
tt = np.arange(int(0.08 * snr.FS)) / snr.FS + 0.37
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(traces), figsize=(4 * len(traces), 3))
lo = hi = 0
for a_, (cell, (mc, md_)) in zip(ax, traces.items()):
    for m, col, lab in [(mc, "k", "control"), (md_, "r", "CNO")]:
        y = m - m[(tt >= 0.38) & (tt < 0.399)].mean()
        a_.plot(tt * 1000 - 400, y, col, lw=1, label=lab)
        w = (tt > 0.403) & (tt < 0.43)
        lo, hi = min(lo, y[w].min()), max(hi, y[w].max())
    a_.set_xlim(-5, 30); a_.set_ylim(-200, 100); a_.set_title(cell, fontsize=9); a_.set_xlabel("ms from pulse")
ax[0].set_ylabel("current (pA), clean sweeps"); ax[0].legend()
plt.tight_layout()

Result: not reproduced. Spontaneous action currents fall into 23 and 18 CNO sweeps of two cells and into 89 of the 100 control sweeps of 6921-2022-09-28-60; the high-passed deflections separate them from the clean sweeps (clean sweeps under 50 noise units, action currents mostly over 100). On the mean of the clean sweeps, the claims file's measure, the amplitude falls in all 4 cells, from 73.1 to 37.5 pA, a reduction of 48.7% (mean of cells), 48.7% (of means) and 54.5% (median), but the paired t test gives P = 0.11 (one-sided 0.056); with the limit at 100 noise units, P = 0.12 and 46.4 to 49.6%. The reductions are 16 points or more from the 30.1% of fig1c, outside the 10-point margin. On the mean of all sweeps the amplitude rises in 2 of 4 cells (P = 0.42), and on the median of sweeps it falls by 42.5% (P = 0.13). In 6921-2022-09-28-60 the current is outward in the 11 clean control sweeps, where the other three cells at -60 mV are inward.

Result: reproduced (resting on an assumption). In the 5 cells CNO does not change the rate significantly: 21.9 to 15.1 Hz, paired t test P = 0.27 (reading b P = 0.23), and P >= 0.12 under both readings at thresholds 6 and 8. At a threshold of 12, reading b gives P = 0.036 (a decrease, reading a P = 0.11). Two cells depend on the threshold: 6917-2022-08-29-58 fires at 55 to 57 Hz in control at thresholds 6 and 8 but 28.6 Hz at 12, and at 27.5 Hz in CNO at 8, so at threshold 8 its control and CNO rates are not counted alike; 6887-2022-07-14-57 fires at 16.5 Hz at 6 and 8 in both conditions, but at threshold 12 its spikes are mostly missed (6.5 and 0.42 Hz). Under reading a, P is 0.11 to 0.27 at every threshold, so the absence holds at all three thresholds (M1: a claim holds under either reading); the one significant result, reading b at threshold 12, comes from the spikes of 6887-2022-07-14-57 missed at that threshold.

fig5d-shrna-higher-rate¶

SNr neurons from mice with ALDH1A1 knocked down in the SNc by shRNA fire faster than control SNr neurons. (Welch's t test, P < 0.001, n = 18 control / 15 shRNA)

shRNA: the control-condition rate of the 15 shRNA cells. Control: the dataset labels no cell as the control of the shRNA or Fig. 5F experiments, so neither reading of the criterion, (a) the control cells as the dataset labels them or (b) the 18 control cells of Fig. 5F, can be identified. The comparison below uses stand-ins that the criterion does not name and is shown only as a variant; sets (ii) and (iii) were chosen after the data had been looked at. The untreated cells it holds are the 49 gabazine-alone cells, which are run as: (i) all 49; (ii) the 31 recorded with the same episodic protocol as the shRNA cells; (iii) the 6 recorded in November 2022, the months of the shRNA recordings.

In [24]:
def control_sets(r):
    g = rates(r, exps=["gabazine"])
    g = g.dropna(subset=["ctrl"])
    return {"(i) all gabazine-alone cells": g,
            "(ii) episodic gabazine-alone cells": g[g.family == "episodic"],
            "(iii) gabazine-alone cells, Nov 2022": g[g.date.str.startswith("2022-11")]}


def group_test(treated, label):
    rows = []
    for r in ["a", "b"]:
        for k in snr.THRESHOLDS:
            tr = rates(r, k, exps=treated)
            sets = control_sets(r) if k == snr.K_THRESH else {kk: v for kk, v in
                   {"(i) all gabazine-alone cells": rates(r, k, exps=["gabazine"]).dropna(subset=["ctrl"])}.items()}
            for name, g in sets.items():
                x = treated_rates(tr)
                y = g.ctrl.to_numpy()
                w = stats.ttest_ind(x, y, equal_var=False)
                rows.append(dict(reading=r, k=k, control=name, n_treated=len(x), n_control=len(y), mean_treated=x.mean(),
                                 mean_control=y.mean(), t=w.statistic, p_welch=w.pvalue,
                                 p_welch_greater=stats.ttest_ind(x, y, equal_var=False, alternative="greater").pvalue))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def treated_rates(tr):
    # the cell's rate in the treatment: the control condition of cells pretreated with the drug, the
    # drug condition of cells to which it was applied during the recording (disulfiram_acute)
    return np.concatenate([tr[tr.experiment != "disulfiram_acute"].ctrl.dropna().to_numpy(),
                           tr[tr.experiment == "disulfiram_acute"].drug1.dropna().to_numpy()])


print(group_test(["shrna_gabazine"], "shRNA").round(5).to_string(index=False))

As a variant only, with untreated gabazine-alone cells as stand-ins, the 15 shRNA cells (26.4 Hz) are faster than the 31 episodic cells (20.3 Hz, Welch P = 0.029), the 6 of November 2022 (17.2 Hz, P = 0.035) and all 49 (21.4 Hz, P = 0.064; P = 0.038 at threshold 6 and 0.14 at 12). The paper's P < 0.001 is not approached by any of them.

# power of the paired t test at n = 3 and 5 for a rise of the paper's size (25%, fig3b) at the
# mean basal rate, with the SD of the change in the gabazine-alone cells (without failed recordings)
g = rates("a", exps=["gabazine"], cl=ok_cells).dropna(subset=["ctrl", "drug1"])
sd = (g.drug1 - g.ctrl).std(ddof=1)
for rise in (0.25, 0.10):
    d_eff = rise * g.ctrl.mean() / sd
    for n in (3, 5):
        df = n - 1
        tc_ = stats.t.ppf(0.975, df)
        power = 1 - stats.nct.cdf(tc_, df, d_eff * np.sqrt(n)) + stats.nct.cdf(-tc_, df, d_eff * np.sqrt(n))
        print(f"rise {rise:.0%} of {g.ctrl.mean():.1f} Hz, SD of change {sd:.2f} Hz (n = {len(g)} gabazine-alone cells): "
              f"effect size {d_eff:.2f}, power of a two-sided paired t test with n = {n}: {power:.2f}")

rise 25% of 21.8 Hz, SD of change 4.26 Hz (n = 47 gabazine-alone cells): effect size 1.28, power of a two-sided paired t test with n = 3: 0.25
rise 25% of 21.8 Hz, SD of change 4.26 Hz (n = 47 gabazine-alone cells): effect size 1.28, power of a two-sided paired t test with n = 5: 0.58
rise 10% of 21.8 Hz, SD of change 4.26 Hz (n = 47 gabazine-alone cells): effect size 0.51, power of a two-sided paired t test with n = 3: 0.09
rise 10% of 21.8 Hz, SD of change 4.26 Hz (n = 47 gabazine-alone cells): effect size 0.51, power of a two-sided paired t test with n = 5: 0.14

Result: reproduced. In the 3 disulfiram cells the dataset holds (the paper has 5), all from one mouse, gabazine gives no significant change: 18.8 to 10.5 Hz, paired t test P = 0.27 (reading b P = 0.19), P >= 0.19 at every threshold. The rate falls in all 3, by 43% on average. One of them, 6808-2022-05-31-45, is a failed recording (data check); without it the 2 cells give P >= 0.45. The test has little power: for a rise of the paper's gabazine size (25%, with the spread of the gabazine-alone cells) a paired t test with 3 cells finds it with probability 0.25 (0.58 with 5), so the absence here says little.

fig6c-snc-gi-dreadd-no-snr-change (blocked by its dependency; test shown)¶

Slowing SNc dopaminergic neurons with Gi-DREADD does not increase SNr spike rate. (P = 0.29, n = 8)

The claims file makes this claim depend on figs3-snc-gi-dreadd-slows-snc (that CNO slows the SNc neurons), whose SNc recordings are not in the dataset, so the claim is blocked (protocol, author step 1.5). Its own SNr recordings are in the dataset (8 cells, DAT-Cre mice with DIO-hM4Di, 10 uM CNO), and the test of the criterion is run on them here: a claim of absence (M6), two-sided paired t test, Wilcoxon as a variant.

Result: reproduced (resting on an assumption). In the 10 GFAP-hM4Di cells CNO raises the rate in 7: under reading b of M1, 14.4 to 18.6 Hz, paired t test P = 0.029, a mean increase of 30.2% (mean of cells) and 29.3% (of means), inside 28 +/- 2.8. The decrease is 11.7%, 11.8% and 8.3% (readings a, b, c of M2; 13.9%, 13.6% and 11.7% under reading b of M1), about half the paper's 23 +/- 2.3%, at every threshold. Without 8979-2025-05-27-164, a failed recording (data check), the 18 cells give P = 0.0099 (reading b P = 0.0082) and a decrease of 10.5%, 11.0% and 7.8%; at a threshold of 12, P = 0.076 and 0.068.

fig7f-snap5114-occludes-quinpirole¶

In the presence of SNAP-5114, quinpirole has no effect on SNr spike rate. (Welch's t test, P = 0.27)

The cells of fig7f-snap5114-decreases-rate that received quinpirole after SNAP-5114 (10). Rates in SNAP-5114 and in SNAP-5114 with quinpirole, compared as unpaired groups by a two-sided Welch's t test (the paper's test as written); a paired t test is a variant (claims file).

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Spikes are detected by a fixed threshold on the high-passed current, not in Clampfit with the paper's (unstated) settings; every rate result is shown at three thresholds, and the significance of some results changes with it, and two outcomes rest on the threshold (marked assumed). The stable window of each condition is taken by the two readings of the claims file, with the drug's application time read as the start of the file the notes name. IPSC amplitudes are measured on the mean of the sweeps of a condition; for Fig. 4A, on the sweeps without spontaneous action currents. The control cells of Fig. 5D and 5F are not labelled in the dataset, so those claims are blocked; untreated gabazine-alone cells are compared as a variant. Seven cell-attached recordings fail during the experiment (the spikes shrink into the noise); they are kept, as the claims file asks, and each affected claim is also given without them, with the same outcome. An eighth such recording, in the SNAP-5114 experiments, is found by inspection, and the two Fig. 7F claims are also given without it.

What was found about the dataset. The condition of each file (virus, drugs, control or drug file) is given only in free-text notes; there is no table of conditions and no record of the light or electrical stimuli. Sixteen files are deposited twice. Three sets of notes do not match their files, among them the nine files of one IPSC cell that carry another cell's notes. The notes give 30 C for every file (the paper: 32 to 33 C) and holding potentials of -50 to -70 mV for the optogenetic IPSCs (the paper: -60 mV). Three subject ids have recordings on dates 4 to 32 days apart. The dataset holds no SNc recordings and no recordings with SCH39166, NPPB, Gq-DREADD, gabazine then quinpirole, low glucose or room temperature, and none of the imaging, RNAscope or voltammetry.
